newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam dong tumbles after central bank band move.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam dong tumbles after central bank band move.

text.p: The Vietnam dong fell sharply against the U.S. dollar in brisk trade on Tuesday following the central State Bank of Vietnam's decision to widen the permitted trading band, dealers said.
Bankers were trading the currency at 11,350 to 11,425 per dollar, as much as 1.9 percent lower than the previous official floor of 11,208 and about the same as current black market rates.
But the currency was still well short of its new floor of 11,650 per dollar.
On Monday the State Bank widened the permitted interbank trading band for the dong to five percent either side of its daily indicative rate from one percent.
Traders said that had freed up strong corporate demand for the dollar, allowing the dong to head sharply lower.
"The market has settled down at 11,350 to 11,400 and there's reasonable business there," said David Pollitt, Treasury Manager for Hongkong Bank in Vietnam.
"This is the first part of a very well thought-out exchange rate policy," he added, saying that the widening of the band would help in squeezing out the black market.
Official newspapers stressed on Tuesday that although the dong now has much more room to move lower, the authorities were not seeking a devaluation and would intervene if it moved too sharply.

"...officials said that the dollar should be closely monitored so that the State Bank could intervene promptly through the interbank foreign exchange market if there were any sharp changes in its value," the daily Vietnam News said.
So far, the central bank has not been sighted selling dollars in the market, dealers said.
"I think they are quite happy with the way this has gone," said one dealer. "They have got a decent two-way market at last and the dong is still some way off its floor."
Others pointed out that with banks now dealing with each other at black market rates, illegal street trade in the dong could be squeezed out.
